newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Azerbaijan's Aliyev backs Turkey oil route.
newsitem.headline: Azerbaijan's Aliyev backs Turkey oil route.

text.p: Azerbaijan President Haydar Aliyev said a decision on the route for the main oil from fields being developed by the Azerbaijan International Operating Co (AIOC) had gone in Turkey's favour, Interfax news agency said on Wednesday.

An AIOC spokeswoman told Reuters the AIOC had yet to submit its recommendations to the government for the routes it sees as feasible to take main oil from its fields located in Azerbaijan's sector of the Caspian Sea.
Interfax quoted Aliyev as saying late on Tuesday that the question of the route "had been decided in favour of Turkey."
"I have always favoured Turkey deep down, and therefore I will do all I can to ensure the oil pipeline passes through Turkey," he was quoted as saying.
The AIOC spokeswoman said that the Baku press was also reporting Aliyev's remarks.
She said that the AIOC had until June 10 to submit its proposals to the Azerbaijan government, and that a further period of 18 to 20 months' study of the proposals was envisaged.
"We have yet to make our recommendations to the government of the (pipeline) options," she said. "But we have no comment at this stage on what the president has said."

AIOC, an 11-member consortium, signed an $8-billion deal in 1994 with the Azeri government to develop three offshore fields. The consortium is led by British Petroleum Plc and Norway's Den norske stats oljeselkap AS (Statoil).

First crude from the project is due to come on stream later this year, and the oil is scheduled to pass through two existing pipelines to Black Sea outlets -- one through Russia and another through ex-Soviet Georgia.
But the lines do not have the combined capacity to handle later peak production, which AIOC expects to reach about 700,000 to 800,000 barrels per day by 2010.
The options being considered for carrying main oil to world markets include routes from the Azeri capital of Baku to Ceyhan in Turkey and pipelines to the Black Sea via Russia or Georgia.
The AIOC spokeswoman said that the company is sticking to its August 28 forecast for the start up of early oil output.
This was in spite of a brief suspension of operations after technical problems arose on April 29 during the drilling of a third appraisal well.
Asked if the problem was going to affect the start-up date, the spokeswoman said, "No, it is not. August 28 remains our target for the first oil production."
